newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil draws $6.0 bln in investment January-May.
newsitem.headline: Brazil draws $6.0 bln in investment January-May.

text.p: Brazil drew $6.0 billion in foreign direct investment from January to May, up 76.8 percent from the $3.4 billion in direct investment that came from abroad in the same period a year ago, the Central Bank said.
In May, FDI totaled $1.74 billion, with most of that coming from the sale of a majority stake in state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
In the period, privatization accounted for $1.163 billion of the total and stock market investments represented some $1.233 billion, it said.
It added that the remaining investment came from multinational companies and other sources.
